# Hack Tracker

> A plain-English tracker of confirmed hacking incidents and outages people suspected were hacks. Official explanations and sources on every entry. Last updated 2026-11-19.

Site: https://hacktracking.com/

## Confirmed Hacks

Incidents confirmed by the affected organization, a government agency, or law enforcement. Most recent incident or news update first.

- [PLAID KARTE customers (MUFG Bank, JINS, Shimamura and others, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#plaid-karte-customers-2026-11) (Nov 13, 2026, Critical): Attackers exploited a vulnerability in servers run by PLAID, the Tokyo company behind the KARTE customer-data marketing service, stole credentials used to connect to its systems and databases, and read data out. They also took over a PLAID account to get into the admin console. PLAID shut down all KARTE services on Nov. 13, and companies that use KARTE have been announcing leaks of their own customers' data since.
- [European Commission HR system (Sysper)](https://hacktracking.com/#european-commission-hr-system-2026-10) (Oct 22, 2026, High): The European Commission confirmed a cyberattack on Sysper, the internal HR platform staff use for salary information, leave requests, timesheets and training sign-ups. Spokesperson Thomas Regnier called it an "AI-generated cyber campaign" first detected on Oct. 22. POLITICO reported that CERT-EU linked the attackers to ARTEX, an open-source AI hacking platform; the Commission has not named the tool.
- [Equinor (energy company, Norway)](https://hacktracking.com/#equinor-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, High): Norway's state-controlled oil and gas giant said it detected an ongoing cyberattack against some of its IT systems and was working to neutralise it.
- [Visa (via third-party provider)](https://hacktracking.com/#visa-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, High): A new ransomware gang called n0n listed Visa on its leak site and set a 48-hour deadline to publish data it claims to have stolen. Visa confirmed an incident, but says it started at an unnamed third-party service provider in the Asia Pacific region. On Nov. 19 the gang published a dataset tied to Visa's premium dining and loyalty programs in Asia-Pacific.
- [JPMorgan Chase (via third-party vendors)](https://hacktracking.com/#jpmorgan-chase-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, High): JPMorgan Chase said third parties that provide services to the bank were targeted in a cyberattack and that the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors. The ransomware gang n0n, which had listed the bank on its leak site, dumped data on Nov. 19 that Cybernews says is tied to the bank's invitation-only Reserve card program.
- [Mastercard (via third-party provider)](https://hacktracking.com/#mastercard-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, High): Mastercard said it was recently informed of an incident at a third-party provider that exposed a limited amount of information from a subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program. The ransomware gang n0n, which also listed Visa and JPMorgan Chase, had listed Mastercard on its leak site and published a dataset after its ransom deadline passed.
- [KPMG Canada (accounting firm)](https://hacktracking.com/#kpmg-canada-2026-11) (Nov 18, 2026, Medium): KPMG Canada confirmed a data breach in which client tax documents were compromised, and is contacting affected clients. It is the latest in a string of breaches at Canadian professional services firms, including several big Bay Street law firms.
- [FFG Industries (Fukuoka Financial Group company, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#ffg-industries-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, Medium): Fukuoka Bank said a third party gained unauthorized access to a data analysis tool used by FFG Industries, a Fukuoka Financial Group company, to compile data from its ordering systems. The tool was set up and run by an outside contractor, and some information in the database it connected to may have leaked.
- [Openlogi (shipping and fulfillment service, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#openlogi-2026-11) (Nov 8, 2026, Medium): An outside party broke into systems at Openlogi, a Japanese warehouse and shipping service used by online stores, on Nov. 8-9 and took shipping data. Store clients including Kashima Antlers FC, United Arrows' overseas shops, REALITY Studios, Toei Animation's online lottery shop and Calpis's butter online shop have since warned their customers.
- [City of South Portland (Maine)](https://hacktracking.com/#city-of-south-portland-2026-11) (Nov 14, 2026, Medium): The city shut down its network after discovering a cybersecurity issue; its preliminary assessment points to cybercriminal activity.
- [Steinberg (music software accounts)](https://hacktracking.com/#steinberg-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, Low): Steinberg, maker of the Cubase music software, says attackers used email and password pairs likely leaked from other, unrelated breaches to break into a limited number of Steinberg accounts (credential stuffing).
- [USEN-ALMEX PreCheck-in (hotel online check-in service, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#usen-almex-precheck-in-2026-11) (Nov 19, 2026, Low): USEN-ALMEX said attackers hit the system-integration API of PreCheck-in, its online pre-check-in service for hotels, with continuous access starting Nov. 14. It found the unauthorized access on Nov. 15 and shut the service down on Nov. 16. Hotel operators using it, including Solare Hotels and Resorts, are notifying guests.
- [Optimizely (website experimentation platform)](https://hacktracking.com/#optimizely-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Critical): Attackers exploited a flaw in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into scripts that run on customers' websites. Researchers at Report URI found the code on 178 organizations' sites, including big names like Salesforce, Zoom, HSBC, CNN and Ikea, so visitors to those sites were exposed without the companies themselves being breached.
- [Irish credit unions (via Wellington IT)](https://hacktracking.com/#irish-credit-unions-2026-10) (Oct 6, 2026, High): An attacker exploited a flaw in the online banking platform Wellington IT provides to Irish credit unions and pulled saved payee records in early October. Credit unions were only told in mid-November.
- [Mitsui Shopping Park app (Mitsui Fudosan, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#mitsui-shopping-park-app-2026-11) (Nov 18, 2026, Medium): Mitsui Fudosan and Mitsui Fudosan Retail Management said a third party gained unauthorized access to the Mitsui Shopping Park app and leaked part of its point-program member data. They found the access on Nov. 18 and suspended the app the same day.
- [Wittenberg-Net (regional internet provider, Germany)](https://hacktracking.com/#wittenberg-net-2026-11) (Nov 18, 2026, Medium): Stadtwerke Wittenberg confirmed that criminals attacked the systems of its regional internet and phone provider Wittenberg-Net overnight into Wednesday, Nov. 18, causing a widespread outage around Wittenberg in Saxony-Anhalt. All relevant systems were taken offline as a precaution.
- [Star Petroleum Refining (SPRC, Thailand)](https://hacktracking.com/#star-petroleum-refining-2026-11) (Nov 18, 2026, Medium): Thai oil refiner Star Petroleum Refining told the Stock Exchange of Thailand it was hit by a cyberattack that gave attackers unauthorized access to company data.
- [StubHub International (ticket resale)](https://hacktracking.com/#stubhub-international-2026-11) (Nov 18, 2026, Medium): StubHub International, the non-U.S. ticket resale business run by Ticketbis, told customers it detected unauthorized access to certain systems between late October and early November.
- [Ethiopian Airlines](https://hacktracking.com/#ethiopian-airlines-2026-11) (Nov 18, 2026, Medium): Ethiopian Airlines emailed members of its ShebaMiles frequent-flyer program warning that some customer information may have been exposed in a recent cyberattack it called "of limited scope."
- [Infoblox (network security company)](https://hacktracking.com/#infoblox-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Medium): The networking and security company confirmed hackers accessed company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor.
- [Osaki Electric (smart meter maker, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#osaki-electric-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, High): Ransomware encrypted data on servers at Osaki Electric, a major Japanese maker of smart electricity meters. The company cut its systems off from outside networks and shut down production systems at its Saitama plant and two production subsidiaries.
- [Nitori (furniture retailer, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#nitori-2026-11) (Nov 6, 2026, High): Japan's biggest furniture chain found intruders in a company system and says customer and order records may have been stolen.
- [Japan health ministry drug supply system](https://hacktracking.com/#japan-health-ministry-drug-supply-system-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, Medium): Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare said NTT Data, which runs and maintains its system for tracking drug supply shortages, reported unauthorized access by a third party. Traces show some stored data was viewed and someone tried to alter it, and a suspicious file was uploaded to the reporting system.
- [SOFT99 (car care products, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#soft99-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, Low): Unauthorized access to an outside company that handles SOFT99's online-shop orders and shipping leaked customer order information.
- [Wilmington School District 209U (Illinois)](https://hacktracking.com/#wilmington-school-district-209u-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, Low): The district's superintendent told families the district was hit by a ransomware attack that may have involved a data breach.
- [International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) website](https://hacktracking.com/#international-ice-hockey-federation-website-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, Low): Hackers replaced the IIHF's homepage with a pro-Russian image and message criticizing Russia's exclusion from international competition. The image was reportedly up for several minutes before the site was taken offline.
- [SBC Medical Group (Shonan Beauty Clinic operator, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#sbc-medical-group-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, High): SBC Medical Group, which runs Shonan Beauty Clinic and other cosmetic and medical clinics in Japan, said attackers got into one of its customer databases after hammering the system from overseas with about 770,000 attempts overnight. It found the intrusion on Nov. 16 and cut the server off the network. Separately, attackers logged into the clinics' accounts on the outside booking service Tribeau (トリビュー) and took reservation data.
- [N-able Mail Assure and SpamExperts (email security cloud)](https://hacktracking.com/#n-able-mail-assure-and-spamexperts-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, High): N-able said unknown attackers gained unauthorized access to a server in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts hosted cloud. A service disruption that started Nov. 16 was first traced to configuration and service dependencies, but the company later determined it was caused by the security incident and disabled management interfaces and APIs.
- [South Korea government email system](https://hacktracking.com/#south-korea-government-email-system-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, High): South Korea's Ministry of the Interior and Safety said hackers got into the government's administrative email system by going through vulnerable local government networks and exploiting a flaw in its single sign-on (SSO) login system.
- [Lighter (crypto exchange)](https://hacktracking.com/#lighter-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Medium): An attacker drained funds from market-maker accounts on Lighter, a decentralized perpetual futures exchange, after the accounts' API keys were exposed. Lighter says the affected accounts used signing code outside its official software kits that reused cryptographic nonces, letting the attacker rebuild private keys from public signatures and move funds out through a public pool.
- [Transport for London (Oyster photocards)](https://hacktracking.com/#transport-for-london-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Medium): Transport for London said it spotted suspicious activity on its Oyster photocard website on Nov. 16, after photocard holders got unexpected emails asking them to create an account they already had. It took the photocard system offline and says unauthorized access to customers' web account details resulted.
- [Charleston County Government (South Carolina)](https://hacktracking.com/#charleston-county-government-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Medium): Charleston County's IT team spotted unusual network activity and the county has confirmed data was removed from its systems. State police (SLED) are investigating on site.
- [Wieson Technologies (connector maker, Taiwan)](https://hacktracking.com/#wieson-technologies-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Low): Wieson Technologies says it discovered on Nov. 16 that some of its information system servers had been hit by a cyberattack, and it isolated the affected servers and network equipment.
- [Canton of Basel-Country administration (Switzerland)](https://hacktracking.com/#canton-of-basel-country-administration-2026-11) (Nov 15, 2026, Medium): Unidentified attackers have been hitting the IT infrastructure of the Swiss canton of Basel-Country since Sunday, Nov. 15, the Cantonal Chancellery said. Some servers were cut off from the internet as a countermeasure.
- [Jeonbuk Office of Education school bus system (South Korea)](https://hacktracking.com/#jeonbuk-office-of-education-school-bus-system-2026-11) (Nov 15, 2026, Low): South Korea's Jeonbuk provincial education office said its school bus management system was hacked on the evening of Nov. 15. It learned of the leak after being alerted by the Ministry of Education's cyber safety center, shut the system down and asked police to investigate.
- [Nikkei (via PLAID KARTE marketing service)](https://hacktracking.com/#nikkei-2026-11) (Nov 15, 2026, Low): KARTE, a marketing service run by PLAID that Nikkei uses, was accessed without authorization, and some Nikkei Online Edition user data it handled may have leaked.
- [Cursor (code editor, via Fireworks AI)](https://hacktracking.com/#cursor-2026-10) (Oct 29, 2026, Medium): Cursor said attackers used an access key stolen from its provider Fireworks AI to copy stored data, then used credentials found in that data to get into other internal systems. On Oct. 29 they used a stolen credential to put malicious copies of a popular extension on Cursor's extension marketplace for about 11 hours.
- [Greiz-Ronneburg district hospital (Germany)](https://hacktracking.com/#greiz-ronneburg-district-hospital-2026-11) (Nov 14, 2026, Medium): A hacker attack on Kreiskrankenhaus Greiz-Ronneburg in Thuringia caused a system failure noticed on the evening of Nov. 14. The district says the hospital received an extortion message on Nov. 15 and calls the attack an extortion attempt.
- [DHC (cosmetics, Japan, via PLAID KARTE)](https://hacktracking.com/#dhc-2026-11) (Nov 13, 2026, Critical): Unauthorized access to KARTE, a marketing service run by PLAID that DHC used for direct mail and similar messages, leaked DHC customer account information linked to it. PLAID notified DHC on Nov. 13.
- [Expedia Group (travel)](https://hacktracking.com/#expedia-group-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, Critical): Expedia Group, owner of Expedia, Hotels.com and Vrbo, confirmed attackers reached its systems through a compromised third-party data platform provider in a supply chain attack that hit several companies. The n0n extortion group claims it stole more than 1 TB of Expedia data. Security researchers had described a similar attack using access tied to the Qubole data platform; Expedia has not named the vendor.
- [RIKEN Fugaku supercomputer (Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#riken-fugaku-supercomputer-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, High): An outsider broke into the internal network that runs Japan's Fugaku supercomputer through a public status dashboard, tampered with internal servers, and took or may have taken user data. RIKEN shut Fugaku down to contain it.
- [OPEN Inc. BizRobo! mini (automation software, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#open-inc-bizrobo-mini-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, Medium): An outside party got into the cloud environment that OPEN Inc. uses to run some of its services on Nov. 12, including the authentication server for its BizRobo! mini automation product. The company spotted a security alert on Nov. 16.
- [Atlas Confit (academic conference system, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#atlas-confit-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, Medium): Atlas, which runs the Confit system that Japanese academic societies use for conferences, says an attacker abroad exploited a flaw in how one optional feature checked users and their permissions, likely found by scanning broadly for weaknesses with AI or similar tools, and pulled presenter information it should not have been able to see.
- [Lyko (beauty retailer, Sweden)](https://hacktracking.com/#lyko-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, Medium): Unauthorized parties got into a small, isolated part of Swedish beauty retailer Lyko's systems and accessed customer data. Lyko says it stopped the breach within an hour and fixed the security hole.
- [Rakuten Securities (online brokerage, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#rakuten-securities-2026-11) (Nov 11, 2026, Critical): Attackers got into a test-environment system at Rakuten Securities on Nov. 11 and customer data held there may have been taken. The company detected the intrusion on Nov. 16 and blocked it.
- [Maersk (shipping)](https://hacktracking.com/#maersk-2026-11) (Nov 11, 2026, High): The shipping giant confirmed that a threat actor breached a legacy system belonging to a company it previously acquired and stole data. The WhiteArmor ransomware group claimed the attack and threatened to release about 100GB of data, demanding $5 million (attacker's claim).
- [Meetsmore (service booking platform, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#meetsmore-2026-11) (Nov 11, 2026, Medium): Attackers logged into 201 accounts using passwords stolen elsewhere, then exploited a flaw in a scheduling feature to pull customer job details.
- [Ipsos (market research)](https://hacktracking.com/#ipsos-2026-11) (Nov 11, 2026, Low): The global market research firm found a breach of one internal information system and filed a complaint with authorities.
- [Vanderbilt University](https://hacktracking.com/#vanderbilt-university-2026-11) (Nov 9, 2026, High): Vanderbilt University in Nashville said on Nov. 9 it was responding to an active cyberattack affecting university devices, systems and cloud-based services, and told everyone to shut down university devices and get off campus Wi-Fi. The BYOD ransomware gang has claimed the attack; that claim has not been confirmed by the university.
- [Apify (web scraping platform)](https://hacktracking.com/#apify-2026-11) (Nov 9, 2026, Medium): Apify, a Czech web scraping and browser automation platform, said an unauthorized third party got into parts of its internal systems on Nov. 9-10. It cut off the access, rotated internal secrets and API tokens, reset all sessions and revoked some third-party OAuth connections, including GitHub.
- [Monadnock Community Hospital (New Hampshire)](https://hacktracking.com/#monadnock-community-hospital-2026-11) (Nov 9, 2026, Medium): A week-long systems outage at the Peterborough, N.H. hospital was caused by a cyber incident, hospital leadership said. Phones and other systems went down and ambulances were diverted from the ER.
- [Trezor customers (via shipping partner Skladon)](https://hacktracking.com/#trezor-customers-2026-11) (Nov 7, 2026, Medium): Crypto hardware wallet maker Trezor says its shipping partner Skladon had unauthorized access to its systems on Nov. 7, and the attacker exported Trezor customer shipping data. Skladon notified Trezor on Nov. 15.
- [Port of Santos authority (Brazil)](https://hacktracking.com/#port-of-santos-authority-2026-11) (Nov 6, 2026, High): A cyberattack hit the Santos Port Authority (APS), the state-owned company that runs Brazil's largest port, knocking its online systems partly offline after a power outage at its headquarters. APS later confirmed a ransom demand. Brazil's Federal Police are investigating.
- [M1 (mobile carrier, Singapore)](https://hacktracking.com/#m1-2026-11) (Nov 6, 2026, Medium): Singapore mobile carrier M1 disclosed a data breach it identified on October 30 involving customer information. It says the breach has been contained.
- [Digital payments firm (Gurugram, India)](https://hacktracking.com/#digital-payments-firm-2026-11) (Nov 5, 2026, Medium): Hackers got into three cloud servers belonging to an unnamed Gurugram-based digital payments firm on the night of Nov. 5-6, ran malicious scripts and abused its payout API to send money out of its escrow account, police say. Two men from Ludhiana have been arrested.
- [Credit Mutuel Arkea (bank, France)](https://hacktracking.com/#credit-mutuel-arkea-2026-11) (Nov 4, 2026, Critical): Attackers got in through the platform of one of the bank's service providers and used Crédit Mutuel Arkéa's own account to send money to other banks, which was then converted into cryptocurrency. The bank suspended some transactions as a precaution and its app was unavailable for several hours.
- [NTT Docomo (mobile carrier, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#ntt-docomo-2026-11) (Nov 4, 2026, High): NTT Docomo detected unauthorized outside access to its Docomo Online Shop and My docomo account site on Nov. 4 and shut down procedures on both early Nov. 5. The company later confirmed that some customer information was taken through the access.
- [2RedBeans (dating site)](https://hacktracking.com/#2redbeans-2026-11) (Nov 4, 2026, High): 2RedBeans (Embrace Inc.) said an unauthorized party got into one of its internal systems on Nov. 4 and copied member information before the access was detected and shut off on Nov. 5.
- [The Kyiv Independent (news outlet)](https://hacktracking.com/#the-kyiv-independent-2026-11) (Nov 4, 2026, Medium): Hackers got into the newsroom's website system and newsletter service, posting and emailing fake claims about Zelensky and Putin. The outlet suspects Russia.
- [SPH Media (news publisher, Singapore)](https://hacktracking.com/#sph-media-2026-11) (Nov 4, 2026, Medium): SPH Media, publisher of The Straits Times, found cyberattacks on five of its systems between Nov. 4 and Nov. 8, which it believes were carried out by the same threat actor. It says software bugs and system configuration played a part.
- [Air Botswana](https://hacktracking.com/#air-botswana-2026-11) (Nov 3, 2026, Low): Botswana's state-owned airline said unauthorized parties got into some of its internal systems in what it described as a suspected ransomware attack.
- [GitBook (documentation platform)](https://hacktracking.com/#gitbook-2026-11) (Nov 2, 2026, High): GitBook says an attacker used a flaw in its SSO login flow to create sessions as GitBook staff, then reached its internal code repositories, a Cloudflare API key and production secrets that gave full infrastructure access. GitBook says the attack appears aimed at one of its customers.
- [Myriad Genetics (genetic testing)](https://hacktracking.com/#myriad-genetics-2026-11) (Nov 2, 2026, Medium): Myriad Genetics detected unauthorized access to its IT network and temporarily suspended testing operations and order management systems while it contained the activity.
- [Barracuda (security company cloud)](https://hacktracking.com/#barracuda-2026-11) (Nov 1, 2026, High): Barracuda said an attacker used a cloud access key it had given a third-party vendor for a past project, and never retired, to get into about 10 of its cloud accounts over 44 hours on Nov. 1-2. The attacker moved through its data analytics environment, source-code repositories and Kubernetes clusters and went after cryptocurrency secrets. Barracuda says the intrusion matched the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework.
- [Ukraine air raid alert app](https://hacktracking.com/#ukraine-air-raid-alert-app-2026-11) (Nov 1, 2026, Medium): Hackers pushed fake nuclear and chemical attack warnings to users of Ukraine's air raid alert app. President Zelensky called it a Russian cyberattack.
- [Binance (crypto exchange)](https://hacktracking.com/#binance-2026-10) (Oct 29, 2026, Critical): Hackers drained about $6.3 billion in crypto from Binance's hot wallets, the largest crypto theft on record. Blockchain analysts traced it to North Korea's TraderTraitor group.
- [ARARA (email delivery service, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#arara-2026-10) (Oct 28, 2026, Critical): Attackers broke into a Japanese newsletter service used by hundreds of brands, including SEGA, and took subscriber email lists.
- [Kyash (payments app, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#kyash-2026-10) (Oct 28, 2026, Low): Kyash says an outsider got into one of its internal web tools for about two and a half hours on Oct. 28 because of an access-control flaw, and may have taken internal documents that included some customer information. It says the Kyash app and card systems were not accessed.
- [WS Audiology (hearing aid maker, parent of Widex and Signia)](https://hacktracking.com/#ws-audiology-2026-10) (Oct 26, 2026, Medium): WS Audiology said attackers gained unauthorized access to its customer relationship management environment and certain operational IT systems. It took some internal and customer-facing systems offline to contain the incident, disrupting the Widex MOMENT app, Widex Compass Cloud and Signia TeleCare for days.
- [University of Texas at Arlington](https://hacktracking.com/#university-of-texas-at-arlington-2026-10) (Oct 26, 2026, Medium): Hackers broke into University of Texas at Arlington systems in late October. The school took down MachForms, its online forms portal for event registration, service requests and surveys, and later confirmed that personal information was stolen. The Qilin ransomware gang claimed the attack.
- [J.B. Hunt (trucking)](https://hacktracking.com/#j-b-hunt-2026-10) (Oct 23, 2026, Medium): J.B. Hunt confirmed it is investigating unauthorized access to certain information in an isolated part of its technology systems. The WhiteArmor extortion group claims it stole data from J.B. Hunt as well as Ryder and Echo Global Logistics; those two have not publicly confirmed an incident.
- [Richmond Public Schools (Virginia)](https://hacktracking.com/#richmond-public-schools-2026-10) (Oct 21, 2026, Medium): Ransom messages appeared on district laptops saying attackers had extracted sensitive data and encrypted critical files, and demanding contact within 72 hours to negotiate. The district took its internet offline, knocking out phones and email.
- [Value Design Value Card (prepaid e-money service, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#value-design-value-card-2026-10) (Oct 19, 2026, High): Attackers exploited a web-server vulnerability at Value Design, a PayCloud Holdings subsidiary that runs the Value Card house e-money service for retailers, and took card ID numbers, PINs and balance data. On Nov. 18 the company said a second server, for a site it runs for business customers, was also hit on Oct. 19 and payment codes were taken from it.
- [ConnectWise (IT management software)](https://hacktracking.com/#connectwise-2026-10) (October 2026, Critical): Chinese state-linked hackers stole credentials from ConnectWise's cloud backup service and used them to get into customers' Microsoft 365 accounts, spying on thousands of companies.
- [NTT Solmare Comic Cmoa (e-book store, Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#ntt-solmare-comic-cmoa-2026-10) (Oct 15, 2026, High): NTT Solmare shut down its Comic Cmoa e-book store on Oct. 15 after detecting possible unauthorized access to its servers, and later confirmed attackers got into its member information system and took data. The store has been brought back in stages, with a full reopening targeted for November.
- [Uber drivers (via Fireworks AI)](https://hacktracking.com/#uber-drivers-2026-10) (Oct 9, 2026, Medium): Hackers breached Fireworks AI, a tech provider, and used stolen credentials to reach Uber data. Notion was also affected.
- [Fandango (movie tickets)](https://hacktracking.com/#fandango-2026-10) (Oct 8, 2026, Medium): Card-skimming code was planted on Fandango's website checkout page and sent payment details typed in by customers to the attackers.
- [IDC Frontier cloud (Japan)](https://hacktracking.com/#idc-frontier-cloud-2026-10) (Oct 7, 2026, High): Ransomware hit a SoftBank-group cloud provider, encrypting customer virtual servers used by companies and local governments.
- [The Japan Times (news outlet)](https://hacktracking.com/#the-japan-times-2026-09) (Sep 18, 2026, Low): Ransomware hit an old administrative file server at The Japan Times' group, and data the attacker claimed to have stolen was later posted online.
- [DriveWealth (brokerage tech)](https://hacktracking.com/#drivewealth-2026-09) (Sep 4, 2026, Critical): An intruder got into DriveWealth's network, which powers investing features in many apps, and accessed customer data including Social Security numbers.
- [IDScan.net (ID verification)](https://hacktracking.com/#idscan-net-2026-09) (Sept 2026, Critical): A company that scans driver's licenses for bars, stores and other businesses confirmed hackers copied ID data from its cloud. Hackers advertised photos of more than 150 million North American drivers.
- [ATF (U.S. firearms agency)](https://hacktracking.com/#atf-2026-08) (Aug 27, 2026, Medium): The ATF declared a "major incident" after a breach of a standalone system holding information on targets of its investigations. A ransomware gang (Qilin) claimed it; ATF has not confirmed who did it.
- [Boston Scientific (medical devices)](https://hacktracking.com/#boston-scientific-2026-08) (Aug 25, 2026, High): A cyberattack knocked out Boston Scientific's global network, halting manufacturing, orders and shipping for about two weeks.
- [fairlife / Coca-Cola](https://hacktracking.com/#fairlife-coca-cola-2026-07) (Jul 16, 2026, High): A ransomware attack on production systems forced Coca-Cola to pause fairlife milk production at all four U.S. plants.
- [Klue (market research software)](https://hacktracking.com/#klue-2026-06) (June 2026, Medium): Hackers used an old Klue credential to steal access keys, then pulled sales/CRM data from many Klue customers, including security companies like HackerOne and LastPass.
- [DentaQuest (dental benefits)](https://hacktracking.com/#dentaquest-2026-05) (May 17, 2026, Critical): Hackers were inside DentaQuest's network for several days and stole personal and health data. It is the largest healthcare breach reported to U.S. regulators this year.
- [Instructure (Canvas learning platform)](https://hacktracking.com/#instructure-2026-05) (May 2026, Critical): The ShinyHunters gang stole data from Canvas, the school platform used by thousands of schools and universities, then defaced login pages during finals. Instructure later reached an agreement with the hackers.
- [Carnival Corporation (cruises)](https://hacktracking.com/#carnival-corporation-2026-04) (Apr 10, 2026, High): Attackers tricked their way into an employee account and copied customer data. ShinyHunters claimed the attack; Carnival hasn't named a group.
- [U.S. water systems (Iran-linked)](https://hacktracking.com/#u-s-water-systems-2026-04) (2026, High): U.S. agencies warned that Iran-affiliated hackers were breaking into internet-exposed control equipment (PLCs) at water and wastewater systems and other critical infrastructure, causing operational disruption.
- [FBI surveillance system](https://hacktracking.com/#fbi-surveillance-system-2026-04) (April 2026, Critical): The FBI declared a "major cyber incident" and notified Congress after a suspected China-linked breach of a system tied to wiretaps and surveillance targets.
- [Stryker (medical technology)](https://hacktracking.com/#stryker-2026-03) (Mar 11, 2026, Critical): Iran-linked hackers (Handala) took over admin accounts and remotely wiped tens of thousands of company devices, disrupting operations for weeks.
- [European Commission cloud](https://hacktracking.com/#european-commission-cloud-2026-03) (2026, High): Hackers poisoned an update of Trivy, a popular security tool, to steal a European Commission cloud key, then took data from its cloud accounts.
- [Cisco SD-WAN zero-day attacks](https://hacktracking.com/#cisco-sd-wan-zero-day-attacks-2026-02) (Feb 25, 2026, High): Attackers exploited unknown flaws in Cisco's SD-WAN network gear to get admin control. CISA ordered federal agencies to patch within two days and hunt for intruders.
- [Poland's energy sector](https://hacktracking.com/#poland-s-energy-sector-2025-12) (Dec 29, 2025, High): A coordinated, destructive attack hit more than 30 wind and solar farms and a major combined heat and power plant. Poland's CERT linked it to Russian state hackers.
- [Jaguar Land Rover](https://hacktracking.com/#jaguar-land-rover-2025-09) (Sept 2025, High): A cyberattack forced JLR to shut down car production for about six weeks. It later reported a heavy loss tied to the attack.

## Speculated / Potential Hacks

Outages or incidents where the public wondered about a hack. These are not confirmed hacks. Each entry includes the official explanation. Most recent incident or news update first.

- [JPMorgan Chase online banking](https://hacktracking.com/#jpmorgan-chase-online-banking-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, High): Chase's online banking slowed and transactions were delayed for hours, with knock-on delays at other banks. It was the fourth big U.S. outage in five days, which fed questions about a coordinated attack. On Nov 17 a new ransomware gang, n0n, listed JPMorgan Chase on its leak site, claiming it stole data; on Nov. 19 the bank confirmed a separate attack on its vendors, which it says is unrelated to the outage. Company explanation given. No evidence of a hack.
- [NSA classified network (NSANet)](https://hacktracking.com/#nsa-classified-network-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, High): The National Security Agency's internal top-secret network went down, right on the heels of a week of big outages, and was still out on Nov. 19, its third day. Official explanation given. No evidence of a hack. Network still being restored.
- [FAA: nationwide ground stop](https://hacktracking.com/#faa-nationwide-ground-stop-2026-11) (Nov 13, 2026, Critical): The FAA halted departures across the U.S. for more than four hours after its air traffic communications network became unstable. It came one day after the big Microsoft outage, so many people asked whether the two were linked or whether someone had hacked the system. No evidence of a hack. Root-cause investigation ongoing.
- [Nvidia (ransomware gang claim)](https://hacktracking.com/#nvidia-2026-11) (Nov 18, 2026, Medium): The Gentlemen ransomware gang listed Nvidia as a victim on its leak site, claiming it would post data soon and giving the company about nine days to pay. It has not posted any samples. Under investigation. No evidence Nvidia's own systems were hacked.
- [Apple services outage (iCloud, App Store, Apple Pay)](https://hacktracking.com/#apple-services-outage-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, High): iCloud sign-in, the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, AppleCare and Apple retail store systems went down for hours, the latest in a week of big U.S. outages. Company explanation given. Not a hack.
- [Marriott Bonvoy sign-in outage](https://hacktracking.com/#marriott-bonvoy-sign-in-outage-2026-11) (Nov 17, 2026, Medium): Marriott.com and the Bonvoy app wouldn't let members sign in for several hours, knocking out mobile check-in and digital room keys for some guests. Company explanation given. No evidence of a hack.
- [U.S. Department of Agriculture applications](https://hacktracking.com/#u-s-department-of-agriculture-applications-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, High): Many USDA applications, including financial tools used for payments to farmers, have been offline over several days. Nextgov/FCW and Government Executive report an internal USDA email saying its security operations center "uncovered a security incident" that required resetting all database passwords and applications. Some staff have also had VPN problems. USDA has not publicly commented. Cause and scope not officially disclosed.
- [United Airlines system outage](https://hacktracking.com/#united-airlines-system-outage-2026-11) (Nov 16, 2026, Medium): Three days after the FAA ground stop, a United system outage delayed departures because pilots couldn't get final aircraft weight data needed for takeoff. No root cause published. No evidence of a hack.
- [Workday HR platform outage](https://hacktracking.com/#workday-hr-platform-outage-2026-11) (Nov 13, 2026, High): Workday's HR platform went down for most of a day starting the afternoon of Nov. 13, leaving employees at customer organizations unable to clock in or out, see pay information, request time off or file for benefits. It hit one day after the Microsoft 365 outage and the same day as the FAA ground stop, during a run of big outages that drew hack theories online. Company explanation given. Not a hack.
- [Microsoft 365 / Outlook global outage](https://hacktracking.com/#microsoft-365-outlook-global-outage-2026-11) (Nov 12, 2026, Critical): Outlook email and other Microsoft 365 services went down worldwide for most of a business day, one of the largest outages in the company's history. Microsoft publicly pushed back on speculation that it had been hacked. Official cause published. Not a hack.
- [American Airlines nationwide ground stop](https://hacktracking.com/#american-airlines-nationwide-ground-stop-2026-07) (Jul 28, 2026, Medium): The FAA briefly stopped all American Airlines departures nationwide after an IT problem. It came during a week of several big outages. No root cause published. No evidence of a hack.
- [Xbox sign-in and game library outage](https://hacktracking.com/#xbox-sign-in-and-game-library-outage-2026-07) (Jul 26, 2026, Medium): Xbox players couldn't sign in, buy or launch games for many hours; even some disc games failed license checks. Company explanation given. Not attributed to a hack.
- [PlayStation Network outage](https://hacktracking.com/#playstation-network-outage-2026-07) (Jul 24, 2026, Low): PlayStation Network accounts, gaming, the store and other features were down for about five hours. Cause not disclosed. No public evidence of a hack.
- [Verizon nationwide wireless outage](https://hacktracking.com/#verizon-nationwide-wireless-outage-2026-01) (Jan 14, 2026, High): Verizon customers across the U.S. lost wireless service for hours. Company explanation given. No evidence of a hack.
- [Cloudflare global outage](https://hacktracking.com/#cloudflare-global-outage-2025-11) (Nov 18, 2025, High): Cloudflare, which sits in front of a huge share of websites, broke much of the web for several hours, including ChatGPT. Even Cloudflare's own team first suspected a massive DDoS attack. Official cause published. Not a hack.
- [Amazon Web Services (US-EAST-1)](https://hacktracking.com/#amazon-web-services-2025-10) (Oct 20, 2025, Critical): A failure in Amazon's biggest cloud region took down a long list of apps and websites for hours, leading many people to wonder if it was an attack on internet infrastructure. Official cause published. Not a hack.
- [Starlink global outage](https://hacktracking.com/#starlink-global-outage-2025-07) (Jul 24, 2025, High): SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet went down worldwide for hours, prompting talk of an attack. Company explanation given. Not a hack.
- [Spain & Portugal blackout](https://hacktracking.com/#spain-portugal-blackout-2025-04) (Apr 28, 2025, Critical): Nearly all of mainland Spain and Portugal lost power. In the first hours, a cyberattack was one of the theories openly discussed. Official reports published. No cyberattack found. (Older event, final report in 2026.)
- [CrowdStrike / Windows global IT outage](https://hacktracking.com/#crowdstrike-windows-global-it-outage-2024-07) (Jul 19, 2024, Critical): A single update from security company CrowdStrike crashed Windows computers around the world, grounding flights and knocking banks, hospitals and broadcasters offline. It is still the go-to comparison whenever a big outage hits. Official cause published. Not a hack. (Older event, still widely referenced.)
